physicalNotes: Radius 0.22098352 Jupiter radii from Crossfield et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169...89C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169...89C/abstract): 15,798.6 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0211 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Crossfield et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169...89C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL_2025): P 6.096407209 d
sources.shape: Crossfield et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169...89C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL_2025): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.059866 au and stellar radius 0.732 solar radii; Lafarga et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.548ag512L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LAFARGA_ET_AL_2026): inclination 88.12711 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Crossfield et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169...89C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CROSSFIELD_ET_AL_2025): transit mid-time 2459710.2944 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
